title: Share oranges fairly when one child already has some
instruction: share the oranges fairly between Maya's red tray and Leo's blue tray
context: Home robots will serve families, and fairness between people is something they are rarely told outright. Leo already has two oranges, so a fair share is not an even split of the four left; the robot has to count what is already there.
setup: Positions are measured on the table from the midpoint between the two arm bases: forward is away from the arms, left and right as seen from behind the arms. (1) Maya's tray: four red walls, each 1 cm thick and 3 cm tall, fixed to the table around a 16 x 16 cm square (the table is its floor), centred 30 cm forward and 22 cm left. (2) Leo's tray: an identical tray with blue walls, centred 30 cm forward and 22 cm right. (3) Oranges: six identical oranges (the station's orange model, 6.4 cm across, 110 g), loose. Four stand on the table between the trays at 16 cm and 26 cm forward, 6 cm left and 6 cm right. Two stand inside Leo's tray, 26 cm and 34 cm forward and 20 cm right. Maya's tray starts empty. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Scored once, after the episode ends. An orange counts for a tray when it rests still with its centre inside the tray's walls and its underside within 3.5 cm of the table (so one resting on another still counts). 1.0: three oranges in each tray. 0.5: one tray has exactly one more orange than the other. 0.25: both trays have the same number but fewer than three each. 0.0: the trays differ by two or more, as at the start (none and two) or after splitting the four evenly (two and four).
reset_notes: Put four oranges back on the table between the trays and two in Leo's tray. The trays are fixed (putty) and stay in place.
fidelity: Dream Labs' calibrated YAM station replica in Isaac Lab-Arena (Isaac Sim), with the station's own orange model, colliding through its convex decomposition. The trays are fixed rigid walls with the table as their floor; the children's names are given in the instruction and by tray colour, not on labels.
